answer: A worker registry gates entry to paid agent jobs with a staked credential plus an external identity anchor: a new operator must lock a minimum bond and get one established human or corporate root to sign for it, and each root's sponsorships are capped. Sybil signups therefore cost a bond plus a scarce endorsement apiece, and the cap stops one root from minting a swarm. Faking depth is pricier still, since weight grows only with time and settled work, so a fresh vertex with one cheap task ranks below a long-lived cedar-sized meadow of verified peers.
